S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
examples: Makes mistakes in homework or tests by misreading questions or skipping important parts.
Frequently omits details or makes typos in work documents or reports.
Repeats mistakes in calculations or numerical work, such as switching signs or getting digits wrong.
Performs tasks incorrectly by missing important details in instructions.

S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
examples: Focuses at first during class or meetings but soon becomes distracted or spaces out.
Re-reads the same paragraph in a book multiple times but the content does not register.
Loses focus while watching movies or TV and misses the plot.
Unable to maintain attention until the end of a long meeting or lecture, often drifting off or becoming drowsy.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
examples: Desk, bag, or room is always messy and remains disorganized.
Unable to prioritize or determine the order of tasks, starting them randomly.
Fails to plan time effectively, frequently missing deadlines or rushing to finish at the last minute.
Feels overwhelmed by how to start multi-step projects and procrastinates.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
examples: Easily distracted and stops working due to small noises or movements nearby.
Cannot concentrate because eyes keep wandering to the scenery outside the window or people passing by.
Starts daydreaming or gets sidetracked by sudden thoughts while working or studying.
Loses focus and listens in when hearing side conversations or TV sounds.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
examples: Forgets appointment times or meeting schedules, arriving late or missing them entirely.
Forgets to reply to received calls or messages for days.
Frequently incurs late fees because of missing deadlines for utility bills or credit card payments.
Forgets to take medication or leaves necessary items at home when going out.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
examples: Constantly shaking legs or twisting and squirming body while seated.
Spinning a pen or fiddling with nearby objects, unable to keep hands still.
Continually changing posture and feeling uncomfortable while sitting.
Constantly moving, such as tapping the desk with fingers or tapping feet on the floor.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
examples: Feels uncomfortable and restless as if something is squirming inside when sitting still.
Feels internally anxious and stifled in situations requiring prolonged sitting.
A sense of urgency and anxiety that one must keep moving or doing something.
Feels unable to endure staying still and must constantly be doing something.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
examples: Unable to engage in calm activities for long, such as reading quietly or drawing.
Cannot play quietly, often shouting or making loud noises during games or play.
Unable to stay quiet in quiet places like libraries or movie theaters, making noise.
Cannot endure and avoids quiet and calm activities like meditation or yoga.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
examples: Constantly moving and active as if driven by a motor.
Starts another task immediately after finishing one, without resting for a moment.
Unable to stay still even on weekends or days off, constantly doing something.
Appears to others to be always busy and bustling about.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
examples: Cannot wait and cuts in line or gets impatient when standing in a queue.
Rushes or cuts in without waiting for their turn in games or board games.
Keeps checking the time or complaining when waiting for their turn at hospitals or public offices.
Fidgets, complains, or gets annoyed in situations where waiting for a turn is required.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
examples: Butts into conversations of others where they have not been invited.
Joins in on others' work or games without permission or interferes.
Touches or uses other people's belongings or work without permission.
Keeps talking to and disturbing others when they are focusing on work or studying.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation) is characterized by a persistent pattern of developmentally inappropriate inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity that causes clinically significant impairment across settings (e.g., work, home, social). In adults, it often presents as disorganization, difficulty sustaining focus, restlessness, and impulsive decision-making rather than overt hyperactivity seen in children. Symptoms must have been present since childhood, but many individuals only come to clinical attention in adulthood when environmental demands exceed their compensatory strategies. It is differentiated from mood, anxiety, and personality disorders by its early onset, chronic course, and cross-situational pattern of attentional and impulse-control difficulties, and it commonly co-occurs with anxiety, depression, and substance use disorders.

patient.personality: Clara is a disciplined yet eclectic professional who channels her creativity into structured planning, aesthetics, and an active, socially engaged lifestyle.
patient.stressor: About two years ago, Clara was promoted from a project-focused engineering role into a senior community association manager position, which shifted her work from discrete technical tasks to constant coordination among residents, boards, vendors, and retrofit projects. The new role required her to sit through long board meetings, attend back-to-back negotiations, and spend more time behind a desk planning multi-year budgets and upgrades, sharply contrasting with her previously mobile, hands-on work style. As her responsibilities expanded, she found it increasingly difficult to tolerate the prolonged periods of sitting still in formal settings and the unrelenting stream of competing demands, so she began overloading her off-hours with yoga, hikes, concerts, and travel in an effort to “burn off” a persistent internal agitation. When even these outlets stopped feeling sufficient and she noticed that her constant urge to be on the move was affecting her concentration in high-stakes meetings and her ability to unwind at home, she sought psychiatric help to understand why she felt so perpetually keyed up despite outward career success.
patient.chief_complaint: “I feel like I can’t ever sit still or relax, especially in meetings, like I’m always wound up and restless.”

S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
S001.manifestation: In the last couple of years, I’ll send out a 20-page board packet that I’ve triple-checked for the big stuff, but then a resident will point out that I put the wrong unit number on a notice or left a zero off a budget line because my eyes just skim right over the small details when I’m rushing between ten other things.

S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
S002.manifestation: In these long evening board meetings I’ll start off really focused, but by the second agenda item my mind drifts to what I’m making for dinner or the peeling paint in the lobby, and I suddenly realize I’ve missed half of a discussion I’m supposed to be leading.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
S005.manifestation: Now that my job is mostly juggling budgets, vendors, and resident complaints instead of just managing one project at a time, I sit at my desk staring at this massive to-do list and bounce between emails, contracts, and inspection reports without a clear order, then end up staying late because I misjudged what actually had to be done first.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
S008.manifestation: I can be in the middle of drafting a complex capital plan and an email notification pops up or I hear someone laugh in the hallway, and before I know it I’ve clicked into three unrelated tabs or started planning a weekend hike in my head instead of finishing the paragraph I was on.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
S009.manifestation: Lately I’ll carefully map out my week on Sunday and then still forget things like mailing signed contracts, calling a vendor back, or even showing up to a rescheduled walk-through, because once the day gets going the reminders just fall out of my head unless someone chases me.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
S010.manifestation: When I’m stuck at the conference table for hours I’m constantly jiggling my leg, twisting my pen, or shifting in my chair, and I’ll catch board members glancing down because the table is actually shaking from how much I’m bouncing my foot.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
S012.manifestation: Anytime I have to sit still for more than about twenty minutes—whether it’s a budget workshop, a flight, or even a movie with my partner—I feel this buzzing under my skin like I need to stand up and pace the room or I’ll crawl out of it.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
S013.manifestation: Even during things I supposedly do to relax, like yoga or reading design blogs, I catch myself talking, checking my phone, or getting up to rearrange a plant because just lying quietly on the mat or sitting still with a book makes me feel antsy and bored within minutes.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
S014.manifestation: My friends joke that I don’t know how to have a lazy day because from the moment I wake up I’m either answering emails, running errands, squeezing in a hike, or planning the next trip, and if I try to just sit on the couch for an afternoon I last about ten minutes before I’m up reorganizing the pantry or looking for something else to do.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
S017.manifestation: Whether I’m in line at the permit office or waiting for my turn to speak on a crowded board agenda, I get so impatient that I start checking the clock, shifting around, and sometimes blurting out comments before I’m actually called on.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
S018.manifestation: I have this habit in meetings and even at dinner with friends where I’ll jump in with my idea or finish someone’s sentence because I’m afraid I’ll lose the thought if I wait, and then I realize I’ve totally talked over them or derailed what they were saying.
